method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Infantile spasms are sudden, brief, bilateral, symmetric contractions of the neck, trunk and limbs, occurring in clusters.** They often belong to one of the commonest severe infant epilepsy syndromes.
claims.source_text: Infantile Spasms (IS), also known as epileptic spasms, is a type of seizure and often relates to one of the most common severe epilepsy syndromes in infants … IS are typically sudden, brief, bilateral and symmetric contraction of the muscles of the neck, trunk and extremities, occurring in clusters
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prompt diagnosis and treatment are critical to limit developmental harm** — over 80% have developmental delay, with high rates of ongoing epilepsy.
claims.source_text: Prompt diagnosis and treatment are critical to minimise the developmental impacts … IS are associated with developmental delay in over 80% of infants, and high rates of ongoing epilepsy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peak onset 3–7 months, but any age in childhood.** Most have Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome: spasms, hypsarrhythmia on EEG and developmental arrest or regression (formerly West syndrome).
claims.source_text: Peak age of IS onset is 3 to 7 months but can occur at any age in childhood … Most children with IS have Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome. Frequently, this is IS accompanied by hypsarrhythmia on EEG and developmental arrest/regression (triad formally known as West syndrome)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suggestive features:** clusters, usually shortly after waking; sudden flexor or extensor spasms of the whole body; **may be subtle — head nodding or facial/ocular movements**, especially early; usually but not always symmetric. **Ask parents to record episodes.**
claims.source_text: Encourage parents to record episodes … Occur in clusters, usually shortly after waking from sleep Typically comprise of sudden flexor or extensor spasms of the whole body May be more subtle eg head nodding or facial/ocular movements, especially in early episodes Usually symmetric, but may be asymmetric
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials:** non-epileptic episodes (shuddering, Sandifer syndrome, sleep myoclonus), benign myoclonic epilepsy of infancy, other infantile epilepsies.
claims.source_text: Non-epileptic episodes eg shuddering, Sandifer syndrome, sleep myoclonus Benign myoclonic epilepsy of infancy Other infantile epilepsies
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common causes:** tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), trisomy 21, focal structural abnormalities, perinatal hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy.
claims.source_text: Common causes of IS include tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC), trisomy 21, focal structural abnormalities, and perinatal hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clues:** a known associated condition; family history of seizures or delay; **early handedness** (focal lesion); dysmorphism; **hypopigmented macules** (TSC); pre-existing delay; neonatal or early infantile seizures; rapidly increasing head circumference.
claims.source_text: Pre-existing condition known to be associated with IS eg TSC, trisomy 21, HIE Family history of seizure disorder or developmental delay (genetic basis) Early handedness (focal structural abnormality) Dysmorphic features or congenital anomalies (chromosomal abnormality) Skin lesions eg hypopigmented macules of TSC Pre-existing developmental delay Neonatal or early infantile seizures Rapid increase in head circumference
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early neurological consultation for every suspected case.** Strongly consider admission where it will speed investigations and treatment.
claims.source_text: Early neurological consultation for all children with suspected IS … Hospital admission should be strongly considered in the instances where it will expedite investigations and commencement of treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent awake and sleep EEG; prompt MRI brain**; if the cause is unknown, genetic testing and a urine metabolic screen.
claims.source_text: Urgent awake and sleep EEG Prompt MRI brain Other investigations for underlying aetiology (if unknown) including genetic testing and urine metabolic screen
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer if urgent EEG, prompt MRI and neurology consultation aren't available locally.**
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Urgent EEG, prompt MRI and neurology consultation are unavailable locally
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment is always neurologist-led. High-dose prednisolone is first line** — except in TSC and treatable metabolic conditions. Dose and weaning are set by the neurologist.
claims.source_text: Treatment will always be led by the treating neurologist … High dose prednisolone is first-line treatment (except for TSC and treatable metabolic conditions) … Dosage and weaning regime should be guided by the treating neurologist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.source_text: Vigabatrin is recommended as first line treatment in TSC
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prednisolone + vigabatrin stops spasms more often than prednisolone alone, but showed no better development at 18 months.**
claims.source_text: Combination prednisolone/vigabatrin has a higher rate of spasm cessation, but showed no improvement in developmental outcome at age 18 months over prednisolone alone
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High-dose prednisolone raises the risk of serious infection and adrenal crisis.** Every child needs a **steroid alert card and a sick day management plan.**
claims.source_text: High dose prednisolone treatment is associated with increased risk of serious infections and adrenal crises. They should have a steroid alert card as well as a sick day management plan
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Febrile or unwell → manage as high-risk under the sepsis guidelines** (immunocompromised). **Vomiting or significant diarrhoea → give IV/IM hydrocortisone** (adrenal insufficiency risk).
claims.source_text: Children with IS who presents febrile or unwell should be managed as per sepsis guidelines as high risk due to immunocompromise … If there is vomiting or significant diarrhoea, administer IV/IM hydrocortisone, as these children are at risk of adrenal insufficiency
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **While on prednisolone:** monitor blood pressure, glucose and weight twice weekly; consider a PPI and prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
claims.source_text: Precautions and monitoring whilst taking prednisolone Monitor blood pressure, glucose and weight twice weekly Consideration of proton pump inhibitor Consideration of prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for infection prevention
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Delay vaccines until one month after ceasing prednisolone**; consider nirsevimab per local guidelines given the degree of immunosuppression.
claims.source_text: Vaccines should be delayed until one month after ceasing prednisolone. See Australian Immunisation Handbook. Consider nirsevimab as per local guidelines due to significant immunosuppression
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admission is usually brief, and discharge does not depend on spasms stopping.** Arrange paediatric neurology follow-up and **a follow-up EEG, ideally two weeks after starting treatment.**
claims.source_text: An admission for IS diagnosis and initial management is usually brief, and discharge is not dependent on spasm cessation … Child has follow-up arranged with a paediatric neurologist and a follow-up EEG arranged ideally two weeks after treatment initiation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give parents the steroid alert card and an individualised sick day plan before discharge.**
claims.source_text: A steroid alert card and individualised sick day management plan should be given to parents prior to hospital discharge regarding treatment in the event of becoming unwell
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Infantile spasms' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Infantile_spasms/, retrieved 2026-09-23
